'''Richard H. Bube''' (August 10, 1927 – June 9, 2018) was an American scientist.

==Academic career==
Bube received his B.S. in [[physics]] from [[Brown University]] in 1946 and his M.A. (1948) and Ph.D. (1950) in physics from [[Princeton University]].<ref name=gale>Richard H. Bube in ''Contemporary Authors Online'', Gale, 2009. Reproduced in [http://galenet.galegroup.com/servlet/BioRC Biography Resource Center]. Farmington Hills, Mich.: Gale, 2009.</ref>

He was a researcher at [[RCA Laboratories]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]], from 1948 to 1962. Thereafter he taught at [[Stanford University]] where he was an [[associate professor]] from 1962 to 1964, when he became professor of [[materials science]] and [[electrical engineering]].<ref name=gale/> He served as his department's chair from 1975 to 1986 and was an [[emeritus]] professor<ref>[http://www.asa3.org/ASA/dialogues/practical-atheists/3-96.htm "How Does My Faith Affect My Scientific Work?"] 48:3, 186, S 1996.</ref> until his death on June 9, 2018. 

For over twenty years he also conducted an undergraduate seminar at Stanford University on "Issues in Science and Christianity",<ref name="ml">Ed. [[J.P. Moreland]] and [[John Mark Reynolds]]. ''Three Views on Creation and Evolution''. Zondervan, 1999. {{ISBN|0-310-22017-3}}. pp.283-284.</ref> until it was cancelled in 1988.

===Professional affiliations===
Bube is a member of:<ref name=gale/>
* The [[American Physical Society]] (fellow)
*The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (fellow)
*The [[American Society for Engineering Education]]
*The [[American Scientific Affiliation]] (fellow, member of executive council from  1964 to 1968, vice-president in 1967, president in 1968, editor of its journal from 1969 to 1983,<ref name=Haas>[http://www.asa3.org/aSA/PSCF/1998/PSCF12-98Haas2.html The Harmonious Dissonance of Evangelical Scientists: Rhetoric and Reality in the Early Decades of The American Scientific Affiliation] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903150842/https://www.asa3.org/ASA/PSCF/1998/PSCF12-98Haas2.html |date=2018-09-03 }}, ''PSCF'' 50 (December 1998): 241-249</ref> emeritus fellow from 2009<ref>[http://www.asa3.org/asa/newsletter/janfeb09/Chapter1.htm Newsletter of the ASA & CSCA Jan/Feb 2009]</ref>)

===Defense of theistic evolution===
In the 1970s, whilst he was editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Scientific Affiliation]]'' Bube defended the viewpoint of [[theistic evolution]] in that journal.<ref name=Haas/>  One such article on this topic would receive in-journal peer-review by [[Baptist]] theologian [[Bernard Ramm|Bernard L. Ramm]], Canadian historian and [[Reformed churches|Reformed scholar]] [[W. Stanford Reid]], [[Fuller Theological Seminary|Fuller]] theologian [[Paul King Jewett]], and Christian apologist [[Alvin Plantinga]].<ref>[http://www.asa3.org/asa/pscf/1975/jasa12-75bube.html#W.%20Stanford%20Reid "Original Sin as Natural Evil"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200724222625/http://www.asa3.org/asa/pscf/1975/jasa12-75bube.html#W.%20Stanford%20Reid |date=2020-07-24 }}. Richard H. Bube. ''[[Perspectives on Science and Christian Faith|JASA]]''. Vol.27 (December 1975):171-180.</ref><ref>Part I of "Original Sin as Natural Evil": [http://www.asa3.org/ASA/PSCF/1971/JASA12-71Bube2.html  "Biblical Evolutionism?"]. Richard H. Bube. ''[[Perspectives on Science and Christian Faith|JASA]]''. Vol.23 (December 1971): 140-145.</ref>

==Personal life==
Bube was born in [[Providence, Rhode Island]], to Edward Neser Bube and Ella Elvira (Baltteim) Bube. He married Betty Jane Meeker on October 9, 1948, and they had four children: Mark Timothy, Kenneth Paul, Sharon Elizabeth and Meryl Lee.<ref name=gale/> His son Mark T. Bube is the General Secretary for Foreign Missions of the [[Orthodox Presbyterian Church]].<ref>''Putting it all Together: Seven Patterns for Relating Science and the Christian faith''. [[University Press of America]], 1995. {{ISBN|0-8191-9755-6}}. p.211.</ref> He married Mary Anne Harman September 9, 2000. He died on June 9, 2018, at the age of 90.<ref>[https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/mercurynews/obituary.aspx?pid=189400336 Dr. Richard H. Bube]</ref>

Eerdmans]], 2001. {{ISBN|0-8028-4755-2}}. pp.147-148.</ref>
